items.title: Marilyn Crispell interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 21, 2022
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] I think of Sun Ra for some reason when you said that. Yeah. Are you affected by music from other cultures? Gamelan and so forth? [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah, yeah. Very much, very, very much, folk music from everywhere...

ctx.x: Well that was with this German pianist Georg Graewe and we just had the idea to do a duo recording. We went to this piano factory to look at pianos and the master tuner there said he was working with all these different tunings and would we like to try something with one of those tunings, and we said yes. That’s how that came about. And I love that recording. It sounds like music from outer space.
I think of Sun Ra for some reason when you said that. Yeah. Are you affected by music from other cultures? Gamelan and so forth?

Yeah, yeah. Very much, very, very much, folk music from everywhere, especially Africa, all the different African countries. Amazing music. Amazing folk music from all over the world really. I also love Scandinavian folk music very much and I remember when I first listened to a recording I was expecting, I don’t know what I was expecting, some like jigs or waltzes or polkas or something. And it was this wild, very like keening across the mountain kind of thing. It sounded to me very much like some Irish folk…
